messages.subject: model scaling
parts:
Hi INLAgroup,

I use the following to scale the model for spatio-temporal interaction type fourth:

H <- inla.read.graph(filename="LDN.graph")
graph <-(inla.graph2matrix(H))
graph <- -graph
diag(graph) <- H$nnbs

Cmatrix=kronecker(rw1,graph)

R=ginv(Cmatrix)
G2=exp(mean(log(diag(R))))
G3=Cmatrix*G2

but the log(diag(R)) produces  NaNs. So I decided to use inla.scale.model function like knmodels.R illustrated "https://github.com/inbo/INLA/blob/master/R/knmodels.R"
to scale the model.

R.t <- inla.scale.model(crossprod(diff(Diagonal(t))),
                                    constr=list(A=matrix(1,1,t), e=0))

R.s <- inla.scale.model(Diagonal(n, colSums(graph)) - graph,
                         constr=list(A=matrix(1, 1, n), e=0))
Cmatrix=kronecker(R.t,R.s)

Am I correct?

Thanks in advance for your help and time.

Bests,
Leila

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] model scaling
parts:
Hi

I think this relates to how 'ginv' defines zero.

INLA:::inla.ginv()

is a modification to 'ginv' which allow you to define 'rankdef=...'
which is the known rank-deficiancy (if you know that). then you'll get
it right, rw1 have rankdef=1, and so with graph (if its connectected),
and then you know the rankdef of the kronecker product.

H
